{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-md-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"33d0b05ac8936c13946a8cee20dd35c8c478d6a73a60772705c3cabeb3ff4d90","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-md-class-c:lineage:51","source_registry_sha256":"fac6b4b22cda98085a5d7df11947d7cc05865e6c877c17be3df4d573863d1518","source_liveness_sha256":"43fe3511474bec2a914f5cdb112291b78f4339942c4d6fb903d9e3bae34bb3fc"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Other important information (equipment, test maneuvers, bicycles, e-vehicles, confusables)","heading":"C2 — Anti-lock brakes, headsets, test maneuvers, bicycle rules and electric low-speed vehicles, with confusables","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Anti-lock brakes, headsets, test maneuvers, bicycle rules and electric low-speed vehicles, with confusables

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A53
When the vehicle's computer senses a wheel locking, ABS pumps the brakes far faster than you could, and you may hear a rumble and feel the pedal vibrate. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A53
You may not drive wearing earplugs, headsets or earphones in both ears, but hearing aids are allowed. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A53
Parallel parking is no longer part of the driving test, though it is taught in the MVA driver education course. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A53
The reverse two-point turn on the driving course test checks the same skills as parallel parking: vision, space judgment, mirrors and signals, steering, braking and acceleration control. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F34 | anchor: A53
On the driving test you must complete pull-in parking, back-in parking and a three-point turn. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F35 | anchor: A53
The test parking is done in a 10 by 20 foot space and the three-point turn in a 16 by 20 foot space. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F36 | anchor: A53
Driving without vehicle insurance is illegal, and failing to insure every vehicle brings fines of up to $2,500 per vehicle each year. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F37 | anchor: A53
Cyclists should ride straight and single file, plan around hazards and opening car doors, yield to pedestrians and obey every signal and sign. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F38 | anchor: A53
Cyclists must ride with traffic on the right side and use the correct intersection lane for left, straight or right. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F39 | anchor: A53
Cyclists should look back before changing lanes or turning and signal their turns. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F40 | anchor: A53
A cyclist may turn left like a car from the left of the lane or a left turn lane, or stop, dismount and walk across in a crosswalk. [A53]
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-F41 | anchor: A54
Braking a bicycle in rain or snow needs extra stopping distance, and pavement markings and utility covers may be slippery. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F42 | anchor: A54
The night-riding paragraph says state law requires a white front headlight and a red rear reflector visible from at least 600 feet. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F43 | anchor: A54
The equipment list says a bicycle ridden at night or in low light needs a white headlight seen from 500 feet and a red rear reflector seen from 600 feet. [A54]
Why it matters: the page gives two headlight distances; see the accuracy flag in D.
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F44 | anchor: A54
Anyone under 16 on a bike must wear a helmet, passengers who are not steering included, and helmets are strongly advised for all ages. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F45 | anchor: A54
By law a bicycle's brakes must stop it within 15 feet from 10 miles per hour on dry, level, clean pavement. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F46 | anchor: A54
A bicycle carrying a small child needs a firmly attached safety seat or trailer, and small items go in a basket, rack or bag so both hands stay on the bars. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F47 | anchor: A54
An electric bicycle runs on human power with motor help, has working pedals, two or three wheels and a motor rated at 750 watts or less. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F48 | anchor: A54
A Class 1 electric bicycle assists only while you pedal and stops assisting at 20 miles per hour. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F49 | anchor: A54
A Class 2 electric bicycle assists whether or not you pedal and stops assisting at 20 miles per hour. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F50 | anchor: A54
A Class 3 electric bicycle assists only while you pedal and stops assisting at 28 miles per hour. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F51 | anchor: A54
An electric low-speed vehicle carries only its operator, weighs under 100 pounds, has handlebars and a standing platform, and runs on motor and human power up to 20 miles per hour. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-F52 | anchor: A54
Its wheels are either one in front and one behind in line, or one in front and two in back, and riders should check for local restrictions. [A54]
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A54
Class 1 and Class 3 electric bicycles both assist only while pedaling but cut out at 20 versus 28 miles per hour, while Class 2 assists without pedaling and cuts out at 20. [A54]
Why it matters: group_hint e-bike-classes; prereq_hint sec12-F47; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec12-F48, sec12-F49, sec12-F50.
Source: [A54 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0054]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A53
Parallel parking is not on the driving test, but pull-in parking, back-in parking and the three-point turn are required. [A53]
Why it matters: group_hint driving-test-maneuvers; prereq_hint none; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec12-F32, sec12-F34.
Source: [A53 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0053]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A52
The rear-facing rule applies under age 2, the child-seat rule under age 8 unless 4 feet 9 inches tall, and the rear-seat advice under age 13. [A52]
Why it matters: group_hint child-passengers; prereq_hint sec12-F20; difficulty_hint 4; confusable_with sec12-F21, sec12-F22, sec12-F28.
Source: [A52 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A51
A supervising driver must be at least 21, while organ donation is open at 18, or at 16 with written parental consent. [A51]
Why it matters: group_hint age-thresholds; prereq_hint sec12-F10; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec12-F10, sec12-F13, sec12-F14.
Source: [A51 -> src:rdmv-md-c:maryland-department-of-transportation-mo:handbook:pdf-0051]
